thread:
mira: Quick sanity check — ran a KV pager sweep across US/EU/APAC with two quant configs (q4f16 / q8_0) and observed unexpectedly high p95 in EU on H100 for seqlen mix >1024. Logs and small matrices attached. Anyone seen kernel switching causing tail here?

 tj: Can you paste the perf matrix (region / GPU / model / seqlen buckets)? :thinking_face: 

 mira: Sure, pasted a distilled view below (from the run that regressed):

 ```
 region | gpu  | model         | seqlen | hit% | p50(ms) | p95(ms)
 ------ | ---- | ------------- | ------ | ---- | ------- | -------
 us     | h100 | rwd-7b-q4f16  | 256    | 92%  | 28      | 120
 eu     | h100 | rwd-7b-q4f16  | 1024   | 54%  | 44      | 420
 apac   | a100 | rwd-7b-q8_0   | 1024   | 60%  | 36      | 240
 ```

 alex: That EU p95 smells like pager thrash + kernel fallback. Could be eviction sweep frequency interacting with the H100 kernel selector so we end up switching from the fast fused kernel to the slower chunked/memcopy path under pressure. Which `pager.*` config was used?

 mira: Default. I tried forcing `pager.eviction_interval=30s` (default=5s) and p95 on EU dropped ~30% but memory footprint went up ~12%. Patch I used: 

 ```yaml
 pager:
   eviction_interval: 30s
   prefetch_window: 512
 ```

 sam: Interesting — quantization direction matters too. q4 should reduce KV bytes, but some kernels pick a different path for q4 vs q8 (e.g., q4 triggers a quant-dequant memcpy for certain matmul kernels). Check `runtime:chosen_kernel` in the trace for the EU H100 runs.

 opsbot: Benchmark artifacts uploaded: https://bench.corp/redwood/kvsweep/2045678901 — includes trace, kernel logs, and flamegraphs. :disk: 

 kevin: FWIW operations: the EU H100 pool was on driver 470.x at the time of that run; newer driver 525.x fixes a kernel selection bug that avoided the memcpy fallback on H100. We're scheduling 525 rollouts next maintenance window. That could explain region divergence.

 mira: Good catch. I re-ran with driver 525 + `eviction_interval=30s` + `prefetch_window=512`. New condensed results: 

 ```
 region | gpu  | model         | seqlen | hit% | p50(ms) | p95(ms)
 ------ | ---- | ------------- | ------ | ---- | ------- | -------
 eu     | h100 | rwd-7b-q4f16  | 1024   | 78%  | 34      | 160
 us     | h100 | rwd-7b-q4f16  | 1024   | 81%  | 30      | 140
 ```

 tj: Nice — so driver + tuned eviction reduced tail. Can we add a gating rule for model bring-up? e.g., fail if p95 > 200ms for seqlen>512 on target region, or auto-suggest `eviction_interval` and `prefetch_window` based on seqlen distribution.

 sam: Also worth trying `runtime.force_quant_kernel=true` on the testbed to force the quant-optimized kernels; it makes kernel selection deterministic for benchmarking.

 alex: Please also record the kernel trace and `nvprof`-like snapshot so SREs can verify memcpy spikes. I suspect the fallback path shows large device-host memcopy counts around eviction events.

 mira: Will do. Adding a short repro script to the artifacts and a note in the model onboarding checklist: "onboard-kv-sweep.sh --model rwd-7b-q4f16 --seqlen-mix 256,1024 --regions eu,us,apac --driver 525 --pager.eviction_interval 30s".

 tj: +1 to adding automated eval. If we can codify a small e2e job that runs on bring-up and posts the p95 and hit% to the PR, that would catch regressions early.

 mira: Agreed. I'll follow up with a PR to the onboarding tests and attach the raw traces from the bench link. Thanks all. :pray: 

 kevin: Ops will prioritize driver rollouts in EU tomorrow morning; will post status here.

 opsbot: CI bench job scheduled: `bench/kvsweep/2045678901/repro-run-1` (queued).
